title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government outlines its approach to AI standards in response to a 2020 Committee report, emphasizing the need for responsible development and use. It commits to creating public standards and regulatory frameworks to ensure safety, transparency, and accountability in AI systems.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains its strategy for monitoring and governing the use of artificial intelligence in qualifications, emphasizing that AI should support, not compromise, fair and accurate assessment. The guidance was issued at the request of key education and trade ministers to ensure AI tools in exams are transparent, reliable, and aligned with national standards.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyright-protected works are used to train and develop artificial intelligence systems and evaluates the impact on creators, industries, and society. It also offers policy recommendations aimed at balancing AI innovation with protecting intellectual property rights.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government replies to the House of Lords report on AI, announcing plans to tighten safety rules, increase funding for research, and create clear regulatory guidance for the industry. It says the aim is to keep the UK as a leader in AI while protecting people and society from potential risks.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document sets out the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee that will examine how artificial intelligence should be governed and integrated into public standards. It also provides a FAQ section to clarify common questions for stakeholders involved in the review process.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into how artificial intelligence should be governed, offering their views on the topic. The submission focuses on key issues such as accountability, transparency, and the development of clear regulatory guidelines to ensure AI is used responsibly.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy examines how artificial intelligence is reshaping rules for medical products, highlighting new risks, benefits, and accountability measures. It outlines steps for regulators to apply the AI White Paper principles—such as transparency, safety, and ethical use—to ensure AI-driven medical devices meet high standards of quality and patient safety.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy outlines a plan to use AI to make the defence organisation more effective, efficient, trustworthy, and influential relative to its size. It aims to guide the development and deployment of AI technologies to support national defence objectives and maintain a competitive edge.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport industry to harness AI’s benefits, such as improving safety, efficiency, and sustainability. At the same time, it outlines measures to mitigate risks like data privacy concerns and potential job disruption.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report tracks how AI developers use copyrighted works, assessing compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It outlines key findings, challenges, and recommendations for policy and practice.
